 North Macedonia v Slovenia Prediction: 5/4 Slovenia to shut out hosts
 Partner Authors
 Updated: 8 hours ago
 With relegation to League C already confirmed in the UEFA Nations League for North Macedonia, it’s only really pride they have to play for when they host Slovenia at Tose Proeski Arena on Monday night. 
 Suffering a 2-1 defeat against Scotland last time out, North Macedonia's winless run continued at Hampden Park.
 Taking on a Slovenia side who still have an opportunity to secure promotion to Nations League Group A, a one-sided encounter looks to be in the offing in Skopje.

 North Macedonia v Slovenia Prediction
 Best Bet: Slovenia to win to nil @ 5/4 
 Without a win since September last year, it's been a torrid run for North Macedonia and their relegation to League C has already been penned in.
 Currently on a six-game losing streak, the Lynxes’ struggles in front of goal have been the real cause for concern for head coach Goce Sedloski.
 Scoring just one goal in their last nine games, North Macedonia have struggled horribly in the final third and it’s hard to see them scoring against a Slovenia side who looked solid at the back in their goalless draw with Switzerland last time out.
 Slovenia came out on top 2-0 when these sides met earlier in this group and a similar scoreline might well be on the cards here.
 With that in mind, a Slovenia victory to nil catches the eye at odds of 5/4 .
 Alternative Bet: Zan Vipotnik anytime goalscorer @ 7/5 
 Set to lead the line for Slovenia on Monday night, Zan Vipotnik is a player worth considering in the anytime goalscorer market for this one.
 Scoring 23 goals in 44 appearances in the Championship last season for Swansea City, Vipotnik has shown how consistent he can be in front of goal.
 Adding another three goals to his collection in the Championship this term, while also scoring for Slovenia against Switzerland in October, Vipotnik appeals at odds of 7/5 to find the back of the net at Tose Proeski Arena.

 While North Macedonia are on this miserable run, it’s rare that they have been blown out of the water in recent UEFA Nations League games.
 In seven of their last eight games, under four total goals have been scored and that trend is backed to continue at Tose Proeski Arena on Monday.
 While it should be a relatively low-scoring affair, Danijel Sturm is fancied in the anytime goalscorer market.
 Sturm bagged a crucial goal in Slovenia’s 2-1 win against Scotland at Hampden Park last month and the Slavia Prague forward is tipped to score another goal on the road in Skopje.
